'''Olinthus Gilbert Gregory''' (29 January 1774{{spnd}}2 February 1841) was an [[England|English]] [[mathematician]], author, and editor.

==Biography==
Gregory was born on 29 January 1774 at [[Yaxley, Cambridgeshire|Yaxley]] in [[Huntingdonshire]],<ref name = "mirror">{{cite journal| title = Obituary. Dr Olinthus Gregory | journal = The Mirror of Literature, Amusement and Instruction | volume = 37 | page = 109 | publisher = Hugh Cunningham | location = London | date = 1841}}</ref> the son of Robert, a shoemaker, and Ann, who also had three younger daughters: Harriet Euphrasia, Sophia (who died in 1783) and Marianna.

Having been educated by [[Richard Weston (botanist)|Richard Weston]], a [[Leicester]] [[botanist]], Olinthus published a treatise, ''Lessons, Astronomical and Philosophical'' in 1796. After moving to [[Cambridge]] in 1796, Gregory first acted as sub-editor on the ''Cambridge Intelligencer'', and then opened a booksellers shop.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911}}

In 1802 he obtained an appointment as mathematical master at the [[Royal Military Academy, Woolwich]] through the influence of [[Charles Hutton]], to whose notice he had been brought by a manuscript on the Use of the Sliding Rule; and when Hutton resigned in 1807 Gregory succeeded him in the professorship.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911}}

Gregory combined his love of mathematics with an interest in music, but not in the melodious sense: music should be subject to rational principles. He proposed "the substitution of proper characters to denote the different kinds of musical time, instead of those vague indefinite ones, which are now in use." No more {{music|time|3|2}} time, or ''Adagio'' and ''Allegro''; rather, some absolute rate, based on the swing of a precisely-calibrated pendulum. Each composition should be played at its pre-defined speed, no matter who was conducting. In discussing Gregory's ideas, Werrett draws attention to the environment at Woolwich in which he developed them, and the use of the metronome to maintain a consistent rhythm in military music.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Werrett|first=Simon|title= Disciplinary Culture: Artillery, Sound, and Science in Woolwich, 1800–1850|journal= 19th-Century Music|volume=39|pages=87–98|date= Fall 2015|issue=2|doi=10.1525/ncm.2015.39.2.87|url=https://zenodo.org/record/56442}}</ref>

Gregory favoured the establishment of a secular university in London. By the end of 1825 he was on a ten-man committee interviewing and selecting the teaching staff. His name was inscribed on the foundation stone of the new university, laid in Gower Street on 30 April 1827.<ref name = "McTutor">{{cite web  | last1 = O'Connor  | first1 = John J | last2 = Robertson | first2 = Edmund F | title = Olinthus Gilbert Gregory| website = MacTutor History of Mathematics archive | publisher = School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews, Scotland | date = November 2010 | url = https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Gregory_Olinthus.html | access-date = 13 April 2020 }}</ref>

Failing health obliged him to retire in 1838, and he died at his home at Queen's Terrace, [[Woolwich]] on 2 February 1841.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911}} Gregory's library was sold on 17 & 18 March 1842 by Southgate & Son of 22 [[Fleet Street]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gray | first1 = G J | title = 415.-Olinthus Gilbert Gregory (390) | journal = Fenland Notes and Queries | volume = 2 | page = 272 | publisher = G.C. Caster | location = Peterborough | date = Jan 1892}}</ref>

The esteem in which Dr Gregory was held can be judged from the following letter in 1841:<ref>{{Citation | last = C. D., M.P. | title = The Late Dr Olinthus Gregory | page = 4 | newspaper = Morning Chronicle | date = 17 February 1841}}</ref>

:''To the Editor of the Morning Chronicle.''
:Sir - I see by your paper of the 11th inst., that Doctor Olinthus Gregory, late Professor Mathematics, &c. &c.,
:Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, has left his widow and family in any thing but affluent circumstances.
:Now, I do trust, that out of the number of people who have experienced his exertions, as a Professor at
:the Royal Military Academy, and also have benefitted by him as highly scientific individual, there may be
:found some who will subscribe to the benefit of the widow and family of that excellent man.
:I remain, sir,
:C. D., M.P.,
:One of Dr. O. G.'s pupils at the R.M.Ac., Woolwich
:[[Edinburgh]], Feb. 13.

===Affiliations===
Many in this list are cited in the [[University of St Andrews]] website.<ref name = "McTutor"/>

*Corresponding Associate of the Academy of Dijon
*Honorary Member of the Literary and Philosophical Society of New York
*Member of the [[New-York Historical Society]]
*Member of the [[Literary and Philosophical Society of Newcastle upon Tyne|Literary and Philosophical]], and the [[Society of Antiquaries of Newcastle upon Tyne|Antiquarian]] Societies of Newcastle upon Tyne
*Member of the [[Cambridge Philosophical Society]]<ref>{{cite journal| last = Gregory, LLD | first = Olinthus | title = An Account of some Experiments made in order to determine the Velocity with which Sound is transmitted in the Atmosphere | journal = Transactions of the Cambridge Philosophical Society | volume = 2 | pages = 119–137 | publisher = Cambridge University Press | location = Cambridge | date = 1827}}</ref>
*Member of the [[Institution of Civil Engineers]]
*Founder member, and later Secretary, of the Astronomical Society<ref>{{cite book | title = Regulations of the Astronomical Society of London: Established February 8, 1820| url = https://archive.org/details/regulationsastr00socigoog| location = London | publisher =  Richard and Arthur Taylor| date = 1820}}</ref>
*Professor Mathematics in the [[Royal Military Academy, Woolwich]]
*Co-founder and first president of the Woolwich Institution for the Advancement of Literary, Scientific and Technical Knowledge<ref>{{cite journal | title = Woolwich Institution for the Advancement of Literary, Scientific, and Technical Knowledge | journal = Mechanics' Magazine, Museum, Register, Journal and Gazette | volume = 32 | page =  106 | publisher = J. C. Robertson | location = London | date = 1839–40}}</ref>

In 1802 Gregory was appointed editor of the ''Gentlemen's Diary'', and from 1819 to 1840 editor of the ''Lady's Diary''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Albree|first1=Joe|last2=Brown|first2=Scott H.|date=2009|title= A valuable monument of mathematical genius : The Ladies' Diary (1704–1840)|journal=Historia Mathematica|volume=36|issue=1|pages=10–47|doi=10.1016/j.hm.2008.09.005|doi-access=free}}</ref> From 1817, "he had the whole of the general superintendence of the almanacks published by the [[Worshipful Company of Stationers and Newspaper Makers|Stationers’ Company]]."<ref name = "mirror"/>

===Family===
On the 4 March 1798, Gregory married Rebecca Gregory (née Marshall; 1769–1807) in Yaxley, Huntingdonshire.<ref>{{citation |title=Olinthus Gilbert Gregory |journal=England, Select Marriages, 1538-1973 [database on-line] |publisher=Ancestry.com Operations, Inc. |location=Lehi, Utah}}</ref><ref name="Gordon">{{cite ODNB |last1=Gordon |first1=Alexander |last2=Marsden |first2=Ben |editor-first1=Ben |editor-last1=Marsden |title=Gregory, Olinthus Gilbert (1774–1841), mathematician |url=https://www.oxforddnb.com/view/10.1093/ref:odnb/9780198614128.001.0001/odnb-9780198614128-e-11469 |access-date=2 August 2025 |location=Oxford |doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/11469 |date=2004 |isbn=978-0-19-861412-8 }}</ref> The couple had a son, James Gregory, and a daughter, Eliza Gregory.<ref>{{citation |title=James Gregory |journal=England, Select Births and Christenings, 1538-1975 [database on-line] |date=June 20, 1805 |publisher=Ancestry.com Operations, Inc. |location=Provo, Utah}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Eliza Gregory |journal=Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths Surrendered to the Non-parochial Registers Commissions of 1837 and 1857 |date=November 20, 1906 |publisher=The National Archives |location=Kew, Surrey}}</ref>

On 20 December 1809, Gregory married Anne Gregory (née Beddome; 1789–1855) at [[St Mary, Stoke Newington|St Mary Church]] in [[Stoke Newington]].<ref>{{citation |title=P92/MRY/021 Olintha [Olinthus] Gilbert Gregory and Anne Beddom |journal=London Church of England Parish Registers |date=December 20, 1809 |publisher=The London Archives |location=London}}</ref><ref name="Gordon"/> The couple had a daughter and two sons, Boswell Robert Gregory and the [[civil engineer]] [[Charles Hutton Gregory]].<ref name = "mirror"/><ref>{{citation |title=P89/ALS/042 Charles Hutton Gregory |journal=London Church of England Parish Registers |date=December 29, 1898 |publisher=The London Archive |location=London}}</ref><ref name="NYT">[https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1898/01/11/102522652.pdf New York Times Obituary (11 January 1898)]</ref> In 1834, Boswell Gregory drowned in the [[Thames]] at Woolwich aged 21.<ref>{{cite news| page = 3 | title = Huntingdon| newspaper = Huntingdon, Bedford & Peterborough Gazette | date = 16 August 1834}}</ref> A poem by [[Letitia Elizabeth Landon]] commemorating Boswell appears in the 1835 edition of Fisher's ''Drawing Room Scrap Book''{{ref|Alpha|α}}.<ref>{{cite book|last =Landon|first=Letitia Elizabeth|title=Fisher's Drawing Room Scrap Book, 1835|url=https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=Bzk_AAAAYAAJ&pg=GBS.PA28-IA4|section=picture and poetical illustration|pages=27–28|year=1834|publisher=Fisher, Son & Co.}}</ref>
